solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Build hotel by Yankee Stadium's entrance? Irritation all round

indicators.note: all round says the irritation word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of Stadium's is used

explanation.surface: A baseball fan grumbles about a hotel built beside Yankee Stadium's gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Build' is the noun, a person's frame, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's build is their bodily shape and size, which is exactly what physique means.

clue.text: The usual sandwiches put out with a spicy snack

indicators.note: sandwiches says the usual word is placed either side of the put-out letters

parts.note: par is the normal or usual level, as in 'par for the course'
KO, a knockout, puts a boxer out

explanation.surface: The regular lunch of sandwiches comes out with a hot nibble on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pakora is an Indian fritter of spiced vegetables in batter, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Country having long border where you find it

indicators.note: border says the long word lies on both sides of the region letters

parts.note: to long for is to have a yen for
the country is found in the ME, the Middle East

explanation.surface: A nation with an extensive frontier, and a note of where on the map it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the country itself, which lies in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a nation at the south-western tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Breather? Gas fitter needs one at the start

indicators.note: at the start says the one letter goes before the rest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen, a gas
haler means healthier, more hale

explanation.surface: A gas fitter is told to bring one of something before starting work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas fitter' reads as a tradesman, but it splits into the gas N and the comparative HALER.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device you breathe medicine in through, so a whimsical breather.

clue.text: A competent note-taker will be fresh!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a good minute-taker is up to taking the minute, able for the job
second meaning: current, the very latest

explanation.walkthrough: The minutes of a meeting are its written record; a capable secretary is up to the task of writing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-the-minute news is the most recent and current, so fresh.

clue.text: Failure overtakes our team again?

parts.note: in a race, to lap someone is to overtake them by a full circuit, getting past them again
our team is us

explanation.surface: A fan worries that the rival team is overtaking ours yet again, a sign of failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' explains the laps: lapping a runner means overtaking them one more time. LAPSUS is Latin, as in lapsus linguae, a slip of the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapsus is a slip or lapse, a small failure of memory or speech.

clue.text: One with craft capsizing in ocean as it rains

indicators.note: capsizing says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sailor's boat overturns at sea in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left out 'in', which says the letters lie inside the phrase that follows. 'craft' suggests a boat, matching 'capsizing' and 'ocean', but it means a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled worker who makes things by hand, someone with a trade.

clue.text: Poet, second Graves, maybe, eclipsing Smart

indicators.note: eclipsing, as in covering over, says the wine word goes round the smart word

parts.note: Graves is a Bordeaux wine, an example of a wine
to smart is to sting, to burn

explanation.surface: A literary ranking with Robert Graves runner-up, outshining Christopher Smart.
explanation.walkthrough: Graves and Smart are both English poets, which makes them look like people here; Graves is the wine and Smart the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian English poet.

clue.text: Substitute pops note with flyer inside ladder

indicators.note: inside says the note and flyer letters go within the ladder word

parts.note: a pair of steps is a stepladder
D is a musical note
a flyer is a leaflet, an ad

explanation.surface: Dad climbs a ladder with a note and a leaflet, perhaps to post them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepdad stands in as father, so stepdads are replacement fathers.

clue.text: Peninsula in America — gas found within thousand kilometre area

indicators.note: found within says the America and gas letters sit inside the thousand, kilometre and area letters

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in 10K
K is short for kilometre, as in a 5K run
to gas is to chat or talk idly

explanation.surface: A geographical note about a stretch of land with gas fields measured in thousands of square kilometres.
explanation.walkthrough: AMCHAT goes between the two Ks, and A follows. 'in America' looks like the location of the peninsula, but Kamchatka is in Russia's far east.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamchatka is a large peninsula in the Russian Far East, between the Sea of Okhotsk and the Pacific.

clue.text: Maybe fighter's fitness trainer who is unusually small

indicators.note: unusually says the letters come out in an uncommon order

parts.note: S is short for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A boxer's fitness coach turns out to be surprisingly short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighter' looks like a boxer, but it is a fighter plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Airworthiness is an aircraft's fitness to fly safely.

clue.text: Once yours truly's heading inside, nearly everyone heads there

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters, so take the first letter of each of the five words before it

parts.note: first letter of truly's
first letter of heading
first letter of inside
first letter of nearly
first letter of everyone

explanation.surface: Signing a letter 'yours truly' and wondering where everyone else is heading.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits 'yours truly', a phrase meaning me: 'yours' goes with 'Once' as the definition and 'truly' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic possessive of thou, an old way of saying yours.

clue.text: Lock where key may be found a hindrance

parts.note: keys are kept on a key ring
a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance', or a let in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a door lock, with the key stuck in it, is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curly lock of hair.

clue.text: China of the future, maybe, appeared a friend of America

parts.note: rose, as in got up or came into view, means appeared
bud is American slang for buddy, a friend

explanation.surface: A forecast that China will one day turn up as a friend of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' reads as the country, but it is the China rose, a garden plant; a bud is that rose before it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is an unopened flower, so a China rosebud is a bloom still to come.

clue.text: Recent order he dispatched for type of hat?

indicators.note: dispatched, as in sent off in all directions, means the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A milliner sends off a fresh order for a particular hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-cornered hat, or tricorne, has its brim turned up on three sides.

clue.text: Time to take in film, ensconced in Peg's sofa

indicators.note: ensconced in says the other letters settle inside the peg word

parts.note: a golf tee is a peg
to eat is to take in food
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Peg curls up on her sofa to watch a film over a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: TEATET goes between TE and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete is an S-shaped settee for two people facing each other.

clue.text: Urge to behave amorously that's taken up at breakfast?

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
to spoon is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Romance blooms over the morning toast.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg spoon is a small spoon picked up to eat a boiled egg.

clue.text: Understood fellow had one position to complete

parts.note: got, as in 'I got it', means understood
he stands for a male person, a fellow
'd is the short form of had, as in he'd
I is the Roman numeral for one
a stance is a position, physical or on an issue

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a man needed one particular post to finish the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To go the distance is an idiom from boxing for lasting to the end, finishing what was started.

clue.text: Willing to support objective when mate approaches?

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting below, so the willing word comes under the objective word

parts.note: an end is an aim, an objective
game means willing, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: Someone keen to back a goal as their friend draws near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' is checkmate in chess, not a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final phase of a chess game, when checkmate is near.

clue.text: Reporter from NSW wrestling with name

indicators.note: wrestling with, as in grappling with, says the letters are thrown about together

explanation.surface: A journalist from New South Wales struggles over a name.
explanation.walkthrough: NSW is New South Wales, the Australian state.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a journalist, someone who reports the news.

clue.text: Working together with popular broadcast's founder?

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is spoken aloud, giving a sound match

parts.note: a ship that founders sinks

explanation.surface: Coordinating with the man who set up a popular radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'founder' looks like a person who starts something, but it is the verb meaning to go down.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in sync means acting in step, in coordination with each other.

clue.text: Betting with gold creating stir abroad, once

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a race
and means with, in addition to
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gambling win in gold coins stirs up a fuss overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for prison; Spandau was the Berlin prison that held Nazi war criminals until it was pulled down in 1987.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandau was a former jail in Germany, so a prison abroad that no longer exists.

clue.text: Blended whiskey to crack open as roast's cooked?

indicators.note: to crack open something is to get inside it, so the whiskey letter goes in

parts.note: a roast is cooked in the oven
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cook splashes whiskey over a joint and opens the oven to check it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whiskey' looks like the drink in the cook's hand, but it is only its NATO-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads inwoven are woven together, so mixed or blended into one fabric.

clue.text: What makes ham have harmful ingredient!

parts.note: add VE and take away the M, NO M, and the word ham becomes have

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what makes ham hazardous to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as VE, NO, M: put VE on the end of HAM, with no M, and it spells HAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is a poison, a harmful substance injected by snakes and other creatures.

clue.text: Letter abroad recalled very different times

indicators.note: recalled, as in called back, says the times are read backwards

parts.note: an age and a mo, a moment, are very different lengths of time

explanation.surface: A letter from overseas brings back memories of very different days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mo' is informal British for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a letter used in a foreign tongue.

clue.text: Price of flat, one brother's acquired

parts.note: even means flat, level

indicators.note: acquired, as in took on, says the brother word holds the one word inside it

parts.note: 'Brother!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone notes that one of their brothers has bought a flat, and wonders what it cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price' is betting odds, not a house price; 'flat' looks like a home but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money is the betting price at which the winnings equal the stake.

clue.text: Vital Geordie heads for Fleet Street?

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in north-east England, NE
Fleet Street is the old home of London newspapers, whose heads are editors, each ED

explanation.surface: A Newcastle journalist sets off for London's newspaper district, desperate for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne; 'heads for' looks like travelling but means the bosses there.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is essential, so it is needed.

clue.text: Man in charge and boy inside: equal before the law?

indicators.note: inside says the boy word sits within the Man letters

parts.note: IOM is short for the Isle of Man
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A man in charge, with his son beside him, asks whether all are equal in law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Isonomic describes isonomy, the principle of equal political and legal rights for citizens.
